global_link_schedule.rule: each cluster-wide LINK starts no earlier than the maximum participant-ready cycle; ready operations within one transaction reserve the physical fabric once in readiness order with trace index breaking ties; participating nodes observe the shared completion, while excluded nodes charge only local instruction issue and block only if a later wait names its completion event

cluster.note: per-node compute, link, collective and idle/skew are reported separately; there is deliberately no single blended cluster number, because the four costs have different physical causes

reporting_scope.note: the functional device counts the architectural work of every node in one transaction and the agreement rule binds the model to that value, so the architectural counters are cluster totals while every timing and memory-traffic figure is one node's share

counters.agreement_rule: every counter outside registry group 0x0c must equal the functional device's value for the same deployment and request

declared.note: sum of isolated costs for each distinct effective LINK subopcode bound to a COMMUNICATION descriptor; repeated uses of the same descriptor/subopcode are priced once, unused descriptors use an explicitly labelled descriptor-only fallback, no mutual contention is included, and the sum is not a schedule makespan or execution measurement

functional_agreement.rule: every counter outside registry group 0x0c must equal the functional device's value for the same deployment and request

cost_table.description: 32-node conventional-chip cluster, v2.  Supersedes abi3-cost-cluster32-v1 in its engine rates only: the tensor, vector and reduction rates are measured, and every fabric parameter, the clock, and the whole memory hierarchy remain assumptions.  No link, switch or endpoint of this machine has been routed or simulated at cycle level.  Generated by tools/build_abi3_cost_tables.py from the artifacts each characterized parameter cites; run that tool with --check to verify this file still matches them.

address_placement.note: descriptor base_address values were distinct and were used

implementation_identity.note: TA-ABI3-OPCONV-1 amendment A7: the blocked contract's association is fixed by an implementation identity -- library, version, device and shape -- and does not claim portability across implementations. Two runs of this identity are bit-identical; a run on another identity is not guaranteed to be

numerics.rule: TA-ABI3-OPCONV-1 amendment A7: anything claiming bit-exactness must name which of the two declared contracts it means, and an execution report records the implementation identity that fixes the blocked contract's association

acyclic_waits.rule: in-order issue plus single-assignment events: a wait is acyclic iff every producer is signalled strictly earlier in program order

bounded_queue_occupancy.rule: issue is credit-gated: an engine descriptor enters a queue only when occupancy is below min(queue_depth, max_outstanding), so occupancy is bounded by construction

no_zero_latency_global_operations.rule: ADR-003 section 9: neither simulator may model a global barrier or collective as zero-latency

engine.reduction.work_per_lane_cycle.name: engine.reduction.work_per_lane_cycle
engine.reduction.work_per_lane_cycle.note: 4096 work units retired in 4103 measured cycles by one engine instance.  one ot_reduction_endpoint instance accepted 4096 reduction.elements in 4103 clocks, measured identically on iverilog, verilator.  4096 flits accepted in 4103 clocks with the downstream always ready; the trailing clocks are the last group draining, so the steady-state rate is the limit this figure approaches from below.  This block has a full place-and-route result in both physical views (results/physical_abi3/sky130hd/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json, results/physical_abi3/asap7/reduction_s8_g2/pnr.json) from the same source file the bench compiled, so its rate and its frequency are the same design and not two.  The hand-written table assumed 1.0 here; the measurement says the assumption was very nearly right, which is a result and not a correction.

engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.name: engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle
engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.note: 33554432 work units retired in 97012165 measured cycles by one engine instance.  one ot_ta_matmul_bf16_sram_engine instance retired 33554432 work units (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) in 97012165 cycles under q_proj_iverilog; the independent q_proj_verilator run of the same campaign took 97010897 cycles, a 0.00% spread on the rate.  Replicated on a second operator: results/tensor_accelerator/qwen3_rtl_kv_proj_campaign.json retires 16777216 work units in 48506095 cycles, 0.345878513 work/lane/cycle.  The campaign's memories are behavioural, so this rate is the RTL's own cycle behaviour under that memory model and not a post-layout timing result; it is a rate, so it is independent of the clock.

This is not one rate for the whole family: a different vector-family engine, ot_ta_rope_bf16_sram_engine, measures 0.135783807 work/lane/cycle in results/tensor_accelerator/qwen3_rtl_rope_campaign.json (5120 work units in 37707 cycles), 1.69x this one.  The table carries the slower of the measured operators, because a family rate that is faster than an operator the family has to run is a rate no run supports.  The campaign's memories are behavioural, so this rate is the RTL's own cycle behaviour under that memory model and not a post-layout timing result; it is a rate, so it is independent of the clock.

schedule_audit.rule: the program carries no tile loops, so every OPERATOR-driven engine instruction must name a SCHEDULE descriptor with a non-zero tile shape; a zeroed or absent mapping is a hard error

tiling.rule: the program loops over layers, token blocks, experts and vocabulary partitions only; one engine instruction names a whole contraction and the SCHEDULE descriptor carries the tile shape, so this model is the only place tiling becomes time

unmodelled_schedule_fields.priority: recorded but not timed: the microsequencer is in-order, so a queue priority cannot reorder anything it issues
